pull.title: rpc: Properly throw on internal I/O errors in GetTransaction
pull.body:
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.

- [x] fa5ad60c32 introduced `test_getrawtransaction_block_data_errors` showing default errors when the block is not available and when the block cannot be read
- [x] fa5b2f13da `getrawtransaction` no longer checks the block availability inline, task delegated to `CheckBlockDataAvailability`, now I/O errors can be detected in `GetTransaction` and thrown

Changes look good to me, left a few nits, I do have a question though;

I wonder if throwing immediately here could prevent callers from trying other lookups that might still succeed for example in `ProcessPSBT`, we first call `GetTransaction` which checks the mempool and txindex, if the tx isnt found we use `FindCoins` to look in the utxo set

But if `FindTx` throws, we never reach that last check, even though the utxo set might still have the input information.

> I wonder if throwing immediately here could prevent callers from trying other lookups that might still succeed for example in `ProcessPSBT`, we first call `GetTransaction` which checks the mempool and txindex, if the tx isnt found we use `FindCoins` to look in the utxo set
> 
> But if `FindTx` throws, we never reach that last check, even though the utxo set might still have the input information.


Correct. But this is intentional: I'd say if someone is running with a corrupt index (or an index with stale data from an unclean shutdown, it would be good to notify them about it as early as possible. This way, they can either disable the index, or recreate it by deleting the index folder. Somehow adding extra fallback code means they'll still run into the issue, just later.

Code review ACK fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c. Good change: a confirmed transaction reported as missing is the wrong answer, and each path that turned an I/O or index error into "not found" now throws instead.

Agree this looks ready for merge, since the remaining suggestions are agreed to be follow-ups: the "OpenBlockFile" wording https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4389790136 and checking the LevelDB iterator status after the `FindTx` scan https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#pullrequestreview-5546709537. The latter fixes similar bugs that happen one level lower at the database layer.

One question before merging: would you want to include the change suggested in [the comment about leftover txindex entries after an unclean shutdown](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4415527729)? If a node crashes shortly after connecting a block that later goes stale, the txindex keeps leftover entries for that block. Before this PR, `getrawtransaction`, `gettxoutproof` and `utxoupdatepsbt` skipped those entries and returned the correct result. With this PR, calls that run into them fail with an internal error, and keep failing until the txindex is rebuilt.

Notes on the [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/traces/35728-fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c-1695-11.html) which mostly covers the same ground as mine: ([unclean shutdown leftovers](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4415527729), [pruning race](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4415333610), [REST test](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4415168040), [`WarnAndThrowErr` linkage](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4415167836)), and has two findings that are new to me:

- [`rpc_rawtransaction.py` could fail intermittently](https://review.fish.foo/traces/35728-fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c-1695-11.html#:~:text=The%20test%20can%20rename%20a%20block%20file%20before%20txindex%20finishes%20syncing). The new test renames `blk00000.dat` before waiting for the txindex to finish syncing, and if the sync reads a block while the file is missing, the node shuts down. Calling `sync_txindex(self, node)` before the rename avoids this.
- [A bad index row can fail `getrawtransaction txid blockhash`](https://review.fish.foo/traces/35728-fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c-1695-11.html#:~:text=A%20corrupt%20txindex%20row%20can%20block%20an%20explicit%2Dblockhash%20lookup). With `-txindex`, the RPC looks in the txindex before reading the requested block, so a bad index row for a different block now fails the call even when the requested block is readable and contains the transaction. Catching the `FindTx` error when a block hash is given and falling through to the block read would avoid this.

It also [points out](https://review.fish.foo/traces/35728-fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c-1695-11.html#:~:text=wording%20does%20not%20match%20the%20RPC%20error%20code) that the release note's "internal error" could be read as `RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR` (-32603), while these errors return `RPC_MISC_ERROR` (-1).

rpc: Return proper error messages from getrawtransaction

When a block hash is passed in and the block can't be read, the RPC
reports "No such transaction found in the provided block", even though
the block was never searched. Fix this by throwing an I/O error from
GetTransaction when ReadBlock fails.

Because the not-found branch no longer runs when the read fails, check
block availability up front with CheckBlockDataAvailability. This also
gives more specific errors for pruned and not yet downloaded blocks
than the previous "Block not available".

Sure, but I don't think we have the review resources to review fixes here (and in all other tests) that are missing the sync. This is already fixed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36618



> [A bad index row can fail `getrawtransaction txid blockhash`](https://review.fish.foo/traces/35728-fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c-1695-11.html#:~:text=A%20corrupt%20txindex%20row%20can%20block%20an%20explicit%2Dblockhash%20lookup). Yes, this is intentional. I think a known corruption should be surfaced to the user, so that they can test/migrate their hardware. Silently ignoring this seems a bit rude toward the user.



> It also [points out](https://review.fish.foo/traces/35728-fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c-1695-11.html#:~:text=wording%20does%20not%20match%20the%20RPC%20error%20code) that the release note's "internal error" could be read as `RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR` (-32603), while these errors return `RPC_MISC_ERROR` (-1).

Sure, but this is a bug in the server to not throw `RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR` on all the internal errors like exceptions from `std::vector::at`, `CHECK_NONFATAL`, or the i/o errors, ...

rpc: Properly throw on internal FindTx IO errors in ProcessPSBT and GetTransaction

Currently, the FindTx return value is an optional, where nullopt
represents two different outcomes: I/O error and missing tx.

One may argue that this is fine in ProcessPSBT, because a -txindex
lookup error is rare, and an error where the fallbacks to lookup the tx
are also failing is even rarer. However, a -txindex corruption may also
point to a larger system corruption and it seems better to notify the
user properly by throwing an exception.

If I/O errors should be ignored in the future, it would be trivial to
catch them here. However, that decision should be up to the
caller, and not enforced by the low-level function.

Do the same for GetTransaction:
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.

Apologies not sure if I understand the question, but what I mean by wrapping in `try...finally` is:
```python
blk_dat.rename(blk_dat_moved)

msg = "I/O error while opening block file via txindex"
assert_raises_rpc_error(-32603, msg, node.getrawtransaction, txid)

# Suppose the assertion above fails.

blk_dat_moved.rename(blk_dat)
```
If `node.getrawtransaction(txid)` does not return the expected RPC error (for example, due to a regression).
Now the code is left with `blk00000.dat.moved`.

So my thought is with `try...finally` even if the assertion fails, the `finally` block executes first, and the node is restored to its original state.

So my initial comment is more of a question; would it be safer if we wrap the assertations in a  `try...finally`.

Hmm, I think the `"I/O error reading block data"` is correct, even when pruning.

The correct way to handle this is to call `CheckBlockDataAvailability` early, and then throw the `"I/O error reading block data"` in `GetTransaction`.

Waiting for the txindex and the blockindex to "fall through" to return a nullptr makes it impossible to uncover IO errors and makes it impossible to distinguish IO errors with normal missing data.

The goal of this pull is to fix exactly that.

(Edit: I've pushed your test draft and my fix)

Nit, only if you push again: the commit message opens by describing the previous error messages and saying it is fixing them, but those messages are actually correct and make sense. The actual bug is described later in the second paragraph: a block that fails to read is reported as "No such transaction found in the provided block". Suggested rewrite:

```
When a block hash is passed in and the block can't be read, the RPC
reports "No such transaction found in the provided block", even though
the block was never searched. Fix this by throwing an I/O error from
GetTransaction when ReadBlock fails.

Because the not-found branch no longer runs when the read fails, check
block availability up front with CheckBlockDataAvailability. This also
gives more specific errors for pruned and not yet downloaded blocks
than the previous "Block not available".
```

Nit, only if you push again: it would help to say why this commit is here, since nothing else in the PR depends on it. As far as I can tell it's an independent cleanup. `ProcessPSBT` repeated the txindex and mempool lookups that [`GetTransaction`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/fa87067c397814f79566f8e1b4f407745e3e1f8c/src/node/transaction.cpp#L145-L161) already does, and it picks up the new errors in the previous commit by calling `FindTx` directly. It is also not a strict refactor, though the difference only shows up on errors: `GetTransaction` checks the mempool first, so a prevout in the mempool is now found without reading the txindex, and an index error no longer fails the RPC for it. Maybe something like:

```
ProcessPSBT repeats the txindex and mempool lookups in GetTransaction.
Call GetTransaction instead, so the lookup and its error handling are
in one place.

GetTransaction checks the mempool before the txindex, so a prevout in
the mempool is now found without reading the index.
```
